# Deterministic-barycenter couplings: exact LPs and an actual-source obstruction

This gives a checkable original-measure mechanism, not a new formulation
equivalent to OC. A coupling supported on one barycenter fiber pays an
actual cap quota simultaneously for ALL base tilts. Mere Minkowski
inclusion and balanced centroids do not supply that coupling, even at an
actual unique deepest source. The exact dual is retained; it is not
silently identified with the physical convex-field capacity dual.

## 1. Fixed marginals and one positive affine base relation

Fix distinct sampled bases z_j, positive lambda_j of sum1 with
sum lambda_j z_j=p, probability laws mu_j supported on compact fibers K_j,
and an actual source Y=(p,y). A deterministic-barycenter coupling means
a probability gamma on product_j K_j with these marginals and

    sum_j lambda_j x_j=y   gamma-almost everywhere.    (1)

The elementary necessary mean condition is sum lambda_j g(mu_j)=y.
It is not sufficient. Convex compatibility only says the barycenter of
EVERY tuple belongs to K_p; it does not say the prescribed marginals can
be coupled so that ALL such barycenters equal one selected y.

An exact quantitative feasibility problem is

    D_y = min_(gamma with marginals mu_j)
                    integral |sum lambda_j x_j-y|^2 dgamma.     (2)

Compactness of the product and of the set of couplings gives attainment.
The cost is continuous, so D_y=0 is equivalent to (1). This is already a
concrete test, with no projective transformation or replacement of sums
by base integrals.

For finite atomic laws mu_j=sum_k w_jk delta_(x_jk), (2) is the explicit
finite LP

    minimize sum_(k1,...,km) cost_(k1,...,km) gamma_(k1,...,km),
    gamma>=0,
    sum_(all indices except kj) gamma_(k1,...,km)=w_j,kj.

Its EXACT finite dual is

    maximize sum_jk w_jk f_jk,
    sum_j f_j,kj <= |sum_j lambda_j x_j,kj-y|^2
                                      for EVERY product tuple. (3)

Finite LP strong duality applies. No convexity, positivity, or common
physical extension of the dual potentials f_jk is part of (3).

The compact-measure version can be approximated without losing the test:
partition every K_j into cells of diameter eta, retain their actual masses,
and replace each cell by a representative. Uniform continuity of the cost
bounds the difference of the two optimal values by its modulus of
continuity on product cells. One direction quantizes a coupling; the other
replaces each atomic coordinate by its original conditional cell law,
independently conditional on the finite tuple. Thus finite LP optima
converge to D_y, and a positive finite dual gap larger than this explicit
modulus gives a rigorous measure-coupling obstruction.

## 2. Original cap credit and an exact marginal-budget packing LP

For any halfspace containing Y, every tuple in (1) has at least one member
(z_j,x_j) in that halfspace. The same holds for outward smoothed profiles,
since a nonnegative physical margin has profile1. Hence

    sum_j integral Psi_H(z_j,x) dmu_j(x) >=1           (4)

for EVERY ambient normal and base tilt. If each marginal is the normalized
uniform law of an original fiber of equal volume v, the original outside
cap mass is at least v. With unequal volumes, (4) safely gives at least
min_j V_j; a larger credit requires an explicit allocation, not an anchor
reuse argument.

Here is a finite LP that retains all original budgets. Discretize the
original measures as atoms indexed by (z,k), with masses w_zk. Choose a
finite collection of tuple TYPES e, each with a fixed positive affine
base relation to p. For each type retain only atom tuples whose full
weighted physical barycenter equals Y. Give each such tuple a nonnegative
mass gamma_e,k. Maximize

    sum_(e,k) gamma_e,k

subject to the usage inequalities

    sum_(all occurrences of atom (z,k)) gamma_e,k <= w_zk.        (5)

Repeated occurrences are counted with their multiplicity. Each tuple
counts at least one captured atom, so (5) proves an actual raw cap quota
equal to the LP value, simultaneously for every through-source cap.
Different tuples may overlap geometrically; their marginal MASS budgets
prevent double charging. This is exactly what the old parity-forest
coincident-copy argument lacked.

The exact finite covering dual has variables f_zk>=0:

    minimize sum_zk w_zk f_zk,
    sum_(all tuple occurrences) f_zk >=1
                                   on EVERY admissible tuple.  (6)

This is a measure-packing certificate rather than a Gamma theorem. Its
feasible tuple list and its budgets can be checked directly. Restricting
to an explicitly constructed family of measure couplings gives a valid
continuous lower bound; arbitrary discretization of equality (1) alone
is not claimed to preserve an exact positive packing value.

## 3. Checkable sufficient conditions

For two equal-weight inputs, (1) holds if and only if mu_2 is the image
of mu_1 under x->2y-x. Indeed the constraint itself forces that map.
For uniform positive bodies this is exactly equality of the reflected
bodies up to null sets (hence equality of the closed convex bodies).

For d+1 equally weighted simplex laws, the archived cyclic barycentric
construction is a useful different condition. If

    K_j=a_j+rT, sum a_j=(d+1)y, centroid(T)=0,
    sum z_j=(d+1)p,

then cyclic barycentric permutations X_j of one uniform T point satisfy
sum X_j=0 and preserve every marginal. The points a_j+rX_j give (1).
The reflected guard example uses two disjoint such circuits and then
retargets actual minimizing caps; see its companion note. These are exact
joint marginal constructions, not consequences of Minkowski inclusion.

## 4. Failure at an ACTUAL unique deepest source

Let T=conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)}, centroid0, and take the actual product
family on complete base {-1,0,1}, all three fibers equal to T. Use any
sufficiently small positive outward smoothing width h and the actual
covariance norm. Let q_h>0 be the own maximum smoothed depth of T; its
unique own maximizer is0 by affine permutation symmetry and the full-
normal singleton argument.

At an exposed endpoint base, finite tilt isolates its own fiber, so its
maximal depth is exactly q_h. At middle mark0, any nonvertical cap has
own contribution at least q_h, and one of its two endpoint base margins
is nonnegative. That endpoint's identical fiber contributes at least the
same own cap mass. Thus middle depth is at least2q_h>q_h. Pure-base caps
also have mass at least2|T|. Consequently all deepest marks have base0.
They lie in a uniform own core for small h, their active caps are proper
and attained, and full smooth normal stationarity gives uniqueness.
Permutation symmetry then fixes the ACTUAL deepest mark at Y=(0,0).

Now consider just the endpoint relation 0=(-1+1)/2 with their FULL
uniform marginals. It has exact Minkowski equality

    (T+T)/2=T=K_0

and exact centroid balance. Nevertheless (1) would require X_+=-X_-.
Since T is not centrally symmetric, uniform T is not its own reflected
law, so no such coupling exists.

There is an explicit positive cost certificate. Every y in T has y1>=-1,
so for all x,y in T,

    |(x+y)/2|^2 >= (x1-1)_+^2/4.

The normalized first-coordinate density of T is (2/9)(2-t) on [-1,2].
Therefore every coupling has

    D_0 >= (1/4) integral_1^2 (t-1)^2(2/9)(2-t)dt
         =1/216>0.                                   (7)

This is a valid dual certificate of the form (3), independent of any
unknown active base tilt. The example shows that actual deepest-source
stationarity and exact Minkowski equality do not manufacture a prescribed
pair coupling. It does not exclude other tuple types or partial packings.

## 5. The physical-field bridge is genuinely additional

If a coupling exists, convexity of a common physical test would give

    Phi(p,y) <= sum_j lambda_j integral Phi(z_j,x)dmu_j(x).

But this inequality already follows from ordinary Jensen whenever the
MEANS satisfy the affine relation; no deterministic coupling is required.
In the actual triangle example of Section4 it holds for EVERY convex
physical Phi, despite the strictly positive coupling defect (7). Thus
these natural physical Jensen inequalities cannot characterize the
coupling feasibility problem or separate its failure.

Some explicit coupling-dual potentials can have convex extensions, but
their integral gap is a barycenter COST, not a captured-boundary ratio for
an actual active menu. Neither (3) nor (6) contains that menu or its
coarea weights. A proof turning coupling failure into a quantified paying
physical field must establish an additional inequality connecting those
objects; it cannot follow merely by naming LP duality.

The exact useful mechanism here is the budget-preserving tuple packing
(5), with its checkable dual (6), and the exact obstruction (7). No
general reciprocal-capacity or OC bound is inferred.
